classification.difficultyReason: Uses supplied partial fractions and a target solution form, fits the growth constant from doubling and solves a logarithmic target-time equation.

content.prompt:
A lake is stocked with 600 fish; the carrying capacity is 12 000. The population $N$ satisfies
$$\frac{dN}{dt}=kN(12\,000-N),$$
with $t$ in years. You may use
$$\frac{12\,000}{N(12\,000-N)}=\frac1N+\frac1{12\,000-N}.$$

answer.worked:
The alternate notation gives the scaling
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dt}{dN}&=\frac1{kN(12\,000-N)}\\\frac{dt}{dN}&=\frac1{12\,000k}\left(\frac1N+\frac1{12\,000-N}\right).
\end{align*}$$
Integrating gives
$$\begin{align*}t&=\frac1{12\,000k}\left(\ln|N|-\ln|12\,000-N|\right)+D\\\ln\left|\frac{N}{12\,000-N}\right|&=12\,000kt+D_1\\\frac{N}{12\,000-N}&=Ae^{12\,000kt}.
\end{align*}$$
Thus the exponent is $12\,000kt$. Using $N(0)=600$,
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{600}{11\,400}\\A&=\frac1{19}.
\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\begin{align*}19N&=(12\,000-N)e^{12\,000kt}\\19N+Ne^{12\,000kt}&=12\,000e^{12\,000kt}\\N(19+e^{12\,000kt})&=12\,000e^{12\,000kt}\\N&=\frac{12\,000e^{12\,000kt}}{19+e^{12\,000kt}}\\N&=\frac{12\,000}{1+19e^{-12\,000kt}}.
\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The population doubled during the first year. Find $k$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find, to the nearest month, how long it takes the population to reach 9000.

answer.worked:
Set $N=9000$:
$$\begin{align*}1+19e^{-12\,000kt}&=\frac{12\,000}{9000}=\frac43\\e^{-12\,000kt}&=\frac1{57}\\12\,000kt&=\ln57.
\end{align*}$$
Since $12\,000k=\ln\dfrac{19}{9}$,
$$\begin{align*}t&=\frac{\ln57}{\ln(19/9)}\\t&\approx5.411\text{ years}\\12t&\approx65\text{ months}.
\end{align*}$$
The population reaches 9000 after 65 months, to the nearest month.
